entities.summary:
Achaean General and Ruler (215–215 BCE)



Achaean General Achaeus was a key figure in the Seleucid kingdom during the Hellenistic period. He was the son of Andromachus and the nephew of Laodice II, who married Seleucus II Callinicus, the father of Antiochus III the Great. Achaeus accompanied Seleucus III Ceraunus on an expedition across Mount Taurus against Attalus I, and after the assassination of Seleucus III Ceraunus, he avenged his death and eventually became a separatist ruler of part of the Greek Seleucid kingdom.



This event had significant regional implications, as Achaeus's actions contributed to the ongoing struggle for power in the Seleucid kingdom.



Achaean General Achaeus is often remembered as a skilled military leader who played a crucial role in shaping the course of the Hellenistic period.
